Fixture: 11_modular_gradient_256x256_lossless.jxl
256x256 smooth RGB gradient, mathematically lossless, effort 7 -- may engage
squeeze/other higher-effort modular transforms

Purpose
-------
Targets slices 5/6/7 (modular decoding, frame headers, end-to-end lossless).
Same smooth gradient formula as 09 (RCT candidate) but larger and at full
effort (-e 7, libjxl's default), which is when the modular encoder has
budget to consider the squeeze transform (progressive Haar-like downsampling
used by modular for large smooth images) and other higher-effort choices
that -e 1/-e 3 would not bother evaluating.

256x256 exactly matches the default group size, so this is exactly one full
group -- it stresses transform selection at scale without also stressing
multi-group tiling. See 12_modular_gray_300x200_lossless.jxl for the
multi-group case.

Provenance
----------
  Encoder:      cjxl v0.13.0 196a43d9 [_AVX2_,SSE4,SSE2] {GNU 15.2.0}
  libjxl rev:   196a43d996aa6ed33ebf98812a7c6d43b2b6d01b (v0.12-snapshot-2-g196a43d9)
  cjxl flags:   -d 0 -e 7
  Built by:     tools/setup-oracles.sh (flags recorded in
                tools/oracle-bin/PINNED_REVISIONS.txt)
  Regenerate:   tools/make-modular-fixtures.sh
                That script IS the recipe; it rewrites the source and re-encodes.

  Source image: tests/fixtures/generated/src_gradient_256x256.ppm  (196623 bytes)
                sha256 746e74c5e9ea016f93f42f1496896f4f4c44d8efee73ad5359b7daa4a9175636
                Synthetic, written by the Python snippet inside
                tools/make-modular-fixtures.sh -- no third-party image was
                used, converted, or consulted. 256x256 8-bit RGB (PPM P6):
                  R = x * 255 / 255    ramp along x (== x, since w-1 = 255)
                  G = y * 255 / 255    ramp along y (== y)
                  B = (x + y) mod 256  diagonal sawtooth
                Same gradient shape as 05_gradient_300x200 and 09, at the
                group-size boundary.

  Fixture:      144 bytes
                sha256 4c2431b6de20c3a3343fb4719bddc79485330c5c1bb5ed1920626e4fde84b140

Verification
------------
djxl decodes it to a PPM byte-identical to the source (checked on every run
of tools/make-modular-fixtures.sh). Classified by `jpxl info` (jpxl-cli) as
a recognized "naked codestream". 144 bytes for a 196623-byte source is a
very high compression ratio, consistent with a smooth, highly-predictable
gradient regardless of which specific transform fired.

Modular features engaged
-------------------------
Not independently confirmed by name -- cjxl printed "Modular, lossless" at
encode time and nothing more specific; jxlinfo is not built in this
checkout; djxl -v / -v -v print no per-feature detail for this stream. The
fixture is *designed* to give squeeze (or another higher-effort transform)
something to find, but whether it actually fired is not verifiable with the
tools available here. See 07_modular_gray_8x8_lossless.jxl.txt for the
general caveat.

cjxl is used strictly as a BLACK BOX: it emits conformant streams for JPXL to
parse. libjxl's source is never read. If a rebuild at a different libjxl
revision changes these digests, that is the point of recording them -- do not
silently update them; note the revision change.
